title: The Zwischenzug
subtitle: The in-between move: recaptures can wait, threats cannot.

steps.say: Zwischenzug — German for 'in-between move' — is the art of NOT recapturing. Your opponent takes a piece and waits for the automatic recapture... but recaptures aren't forced. If you have a check or a bigger capture available, play it FIRST and recapture later. This one habit — pausing before every recapture — wins more material at club level than any tactic.

steps.prompt: Black just captured your knight on c3, expecting bxc3. Both bishops hang — but don't recapture yet. Find the in-between blow!
hints: Before recapturing, scan your own captures: what does your g5 bishop see down its diagonal?
Bxd8! Take the QUEEN first — Black must recapture, and only then do you take the c3 bishop.

line.say: The zwischenzug — while your opponent waited for bxc3, you took the most valuable piece on the board!
NOW the recapture, at your leisure. Count it: you gave a knight and a bishop, and won a bishop and a QUEEN. The 'automatic' bxc3 would have left the trade dead even.

rejections.say: Qxg5! — the reflex recapture, and Black's queen calmly takes your bishop: dead-even trade. Your g5 bishop was staring at the queen the whole time. Recaptures can WAIT.

steps.wrongSay: Two of your pieces can capture something. One target is worth nine points. Take THAT one first.
steps.successSay: The pause before recapturing — from today, make it a permanent habit.

steps.prompt: Trade tension: your d5 knight is attacked by the c6 pawn, and Black's g4 knight hangs to your h3 pawn. Everyone expects the swap-off. Squeeze an extra pawn out of it!
hints: Your knight is doomed anyway — so before it dies, can it TAKE something? With check, even?
Nxe7+! The doomed knight grabs a pawn with check — then you capture on g4, and when Black rounds up your knight, you're a clean pawn ahead.

line.say: The desperado zwischenzug — the knight was lost anyway, so it sells itself for a pawn WITH CHECK, buying the tempo for...

...the capture on g4. Black will now win your e7 knight back with Qxe7 — but total the ledger: knight for knight, plus the e7 pawn in your pocket. The 'obvious' hxg4 first would have netted exactly nothing.

rejections.say: cxd5 — knights traded, material even, opportunity gone. Your d5 knight was doomed: doomed pieces should always grab something on the way out. Nxe7+!

steps.wrongSay: Your knight can't be saved — so make its last move count. Check the pawns it can reach.
steps.successSay: Doomed piece + in-between capture = free material. This exact pattern appears in half of all club-level trades.

steps.say: The zwischenzug checklist, before EVERY recapture: (1) Do I have a check? (2) Do I have a capture of something bigger? (3) Is there a mate threat? Only when all three answers are 'no' do you recapture. Your opponents recapture automatically — that half-second pause is your edge.
